title: Polling results on capitalism and socialism - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Polling cited from Mene Ukueberuwa at The Free Press finds Americans souring on capitalism (only a third privately positive) while remaining wary of full socialism, with large gaps between what respondents say publicly versus privately across party, gender, race, and income.

insights.claim: Only a third of Americans privately say they have a positive view of capitalism, per polling reported by The Free Press.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A weak private base of support for capitalism signals durable political risk to pro-market policy.
insights.quote: Just a third of Americans privately say they have a positive view of capitalism.

insights.claim: Less than half of Republicans privately express a positive view of capitalism, even though two-thirds support it in public.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Private ambivalence among capitalism's expected base suggests softer support than headline partisan numbers imply.
insights.quote: Less than half of Republicans privately express a positive view of capitalism, though two-thirds support it in public.

insights.claim: Almost half of women privately say they would consider voting for a socialist, and 58 percent of people earning over $150,000 privately say they are open to voting for a socialist versus 42 percent publicly.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Openness to socialist candidates extends into high-income cohorts, widening the potential coalition beyond the usual base.
insights.quote: Of people earning more than $150,000 a year, 58 percent privately say they are open to voting for a socialist, though only 42 percent say so publicly.
insights.locator: Of people earning more than $150,000 a year

insights.claim: Nearly a third of Gen Z publicly say America would be better off as a socialist country, but only 14 percent say so in private, a reverse of the usual social-desirability direction.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Suggests youth socialism may be partly performative, tempering how much it reflects real electoral behavior.
insights.quote: Nearly a third of Gen Z publicly say that America would be better off as a socialist country, but only 14 percent say so in private.
insights.locator: Nearly a third of Gen Z publicly say

insights.claim: A majority of blacks publicly say capitalism causes America's social ills, but only 37 percent say so privately, another large public-private gap.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Preference-falsification gaps across groups mean public polling on capitalism may overstate genuine hostility.
insights.quote: The majority of blacks publicly say capitalism is the cause of America’s social ills, but only 37 percent say so privately.
